sovereign_country.strategic_role: 泛欧数字贸易门户、极速低成本在线设立与新锐EMI银行开户

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Endowment Management for Philanthropic and Scientific Grants

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English-derived; offshore special-territory statutory overlay)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: UK–Gibraltar double taxation relief arrangement on taxes on income (long-standing arrangement, as supplemented by later exchanges of notes)
UK–Gibraltar Tax Co-operation arrangements (exchange of information and anti-avoidance alignment instruments concluded in 2018–2019)
Convention between Malta and Gibraltar for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force since 2019)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended to Gibraltar via the United Kingdom)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar), as amended by the Proceeds of Crime (Amendment) Act 2016 and the Proceeds of Crime (Amendment) Act 2020; FSC AML/CFT Rulebook (2019, as revised); Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) beneficial-ownership provisions requiring the maintenance and filing of a register of persons with significant control for the central UBO register; Limited Partnerships Act 1883 (Gibraltar), as amended by the Limited Partnerships (Amendment) Act 2014, extending beneficial-ownership record-keeping duties to exempted limited partnerships; Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2016 (as amended); mandatory screening references include the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list and HM Treasury UK Sanctions List.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and certificate of good standing of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry / registrar of the general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / current register of directors and members of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent / corporate service provider of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or UK consular legalization where the issuer is located in a non-Hague-Convention state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and proof of residential address of each individual general partner and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed notary public of the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-endowment evidence for the contributed charitable corpus
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance department of the issuing banking institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legal opinion / no-lien certificate with respect to the endowment funds to be contributed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified external legal counsel in the originator's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all general partners, limited partners, beneficial owners and grant-committee appointees against the OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, HM Treasury's UK Sanctions List and the sanctions list administered by the Gibraltar Sanctions Office (Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2016, as amended). PEP status is determined per FATF Standards and the FSC AML/CFT Rulebook; incumbent PEPs, family members and close associates attract enhanced due diligence with mandatory source-of-wealth verification; any hit or ambiguity is escalated as a suspicious activity report under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies House Gibraltar (Registry of Companies) - online name search and reservation portal: companieshouse.gi
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the sole official language; the exempted limited partnership name must be in Latin script and must end with 'Exempted Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'ELP'. Non-Latin-script or translated names require a certified transliteration into Latin characters; the Registrar applies the phonetic-confusion and visual-similarity test against the existing register.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Limited Partnerships Act 2015, ss. 1-45; Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015, ss. 1-28; Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 179) ss. 16-20 (as applicable to the corporate general partner); Charities Act 1962, ss. 3-8 (charitable designation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Official Registry: Gibraltar Registry of Companies, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, 10/21 Cathedral Square, Gibraltar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration as an Exempted Limited Partnership (Form ELP-1) together with the Limited Partnership Agreement and General Partner Declaration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital for an Exempted Limited Partnership; capital is set by the Limited Partnership Agreement. Charitable endowment assets must be held in a segregated fiduciary account; no escrow requirement is mandated for formation, but the General Partner must evidence source of funds in the onboarding docket.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the undersigned corporate general partner of the ELP (a) approves the subscription of partnership capital, authorized at GBP 1,000 in the first instance, representing the charitable endowment seed corpus; (b) adopts the registered office situated at the licensed address provided by the licensed fiduciary service provider, to be filed with the Gibraltar Registry of Companies; (c) appoints the initial corporate general partner and its nominee directors, and a qualified licensed manager as the first designated official for AML compliance; and (d) authorizes the execution and submission of all incorporation filings to the Registrar of Companies, the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, and any other regulatory body as required for the lawful commencement of grant-making operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registry of Companies, Applications and Filings Window, via the e-Recordal online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request using Form RES-01 through the Companies Registry electronic system or in person at the Registry counter. The proposed name must include the expression 'Exempted Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'ELP' unless otherwise exempted. For a charitable foundation, obtain a non-binding pre-clearance from the Gibraltar Charity Commissioner for the word 'foundation' or 'charitable' in the name.
required_dossiers: Completed Form RES-01
Passport copy of the proposed general partner
Short description of the intended charitable purpose
Consent letter from the registered agent (if the name includes 'foundation')
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of similarity or undesirability, the applicant may submit a revised name with a written explanation of distinguishing elements, or appeal the refusal to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days under the Companies (Names) Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and Charitable Objects Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public, Gibraltar Law Society; supervised by the appointed licensed fiduciary service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Gibraltar-licensed legal or fiduciary professional to draft the Limited Partnership Agreement and a separate Charitable Objects Declaration, specifying grant-making powers, endowment investment restrictions, and dissolution distribution rules. Execute all instruments before a Gibraltar Notary Public; if any party is outside Gibraltar, execute before a foreign notary and obtain an Apostille certificate from the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (or the notary's competent authority under the Hague Convention).
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement (English version)
Charitable Objects Declaration
Certified passports of partners
Proof of source of funds for initial endowment
Notarized power of attorney if signing through a representative
Apostille certificate for foreign-issued documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry or the fiduciary service provider queries the partnership deed for missing clauses, the legal professional will issue a supplemental deed of amendment, re-executed with notarization, and file it as a supplementary instrument to the original application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration Filing with the Gibraltar Registry of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registry of Companies, Official Registration Window; system: GFSC e-Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form ELP-1 electronically or at the Registry counter, enclosing the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, the Charitable Objects Declaration, the statement of compliance signed by the general partner, and the prescribed registration fee. Pay via bank transfer or card. The Registrar will examine the instrument for statutory conformity and issue the Certificate of Registration as an Exempted Limited Partnership. The certificate defines the date of legal formation.
required_dossiers: Form ELP-1 (Application for Registration)
Original or certified copy of the executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Statement of Compliance (Form ELP-2)
Charitable Objects Declaration (for the foundation endorsement)
Registered office consent form (from the local registered office provider)
Filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried for incomplete information, the Registry will issue a notice of defect. The applicant has 10 working days to respond by filing an amendment or additional evidence. A rejected filing may be refiled without prejudice after payment of a resubmission fee (currently GBP 50).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of the corporate general partner, registered office and statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registry of Companies; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (for the corporate general partner licensing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the corporate general partner is a Gibraltar-incorporated or otherwise permitted non-resident company with a registered agent in Gibraltar. Pass resolutions to adopt the registered office at the licensed provider's physical premises and to appoint the first compliance officer and a licensed manager (if required). File the 'General Partner and Officer Details' return (Form GP-01) with the Registry. The appointments take effect immediately on filing of the return.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of the corporate general partner
Corporate resolutions of the general partner appointing officers
Registered office consent agreement
AML/CFT compliance officer appointment letter
Form GP-01 (notice of general partner and officers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry or GFSC objects to an officer (e.g. for lack of fitness and propriety), the ELP may substitute the officer by filing Form GP-02 with a revised consent letter and a declaration of fitness; no additional fee is triggered if filed within 7 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Post-Incorporation Filings and Availability to Commence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registry of Companies; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission; Gibraltar Income Tax Office (exempt status management)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate is issued, draft and file with the Registry: (a) the notice of the initial registered office (if different from the adoption date), (b) the first Statutory Declaration of Compliance with the Exempted Limited Partnerships Act, and (c) the application for exemption from income tax under the Income Tax (Exempt Companies) Regulations, if elected. Obtain the certified certificate and proceed to open the segregated bank account for the endowment. Filing of these documents completes the statutory formation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration (ELP)
Form SD-ELP (statutory declaration)
Application for income tax exemption (Form E-1)
Bank account opening document pack for the endowment account
Application for charitable registration with the Gibraltar Charity Commissioner (for grant disbursement powers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax exemption application is queried for missing documentation, the registrar will allow rectification within 21 days. If the charitable registration is refused, the entity may operate purely as a private endowment trust until the appeal before the Charities Appeal Tribunal is concluded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) – Authorisation and Licensing Division; and the Gibraltar Charity Commissioner for the charitable endowment/grants sphere
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Financial Services (Private Charitable Endowment) Licence – Class 4 (Grant Distribution and Endowment Management)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (DESCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Registration / Exempt from Full EIA (office-based activity with no industrial emissions; only fit-out works permitted)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If only office activities and grant disbursement: no point-source wastewater discharges; all liquid wastes to be handled under the Gibraltar Trade Effluent Standards, suspended solids < 30 mg/L, pH 6-9; no VOC or particulate emissions. Any minor server room backup generator must meet the Control of Noise and Emissions Limits Regulations and the Clean Air Act requirements with particulate matter < 10 µg/m3. Waste management must be contracted to an authorised waste carrier under the Waste Management Act 2016.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service under the Fire Safety (Places of Work) Regulations; structural load and public safety inspection by the Building Control Office, HM Government of Gibraltar; and workplace clearance for the registered office (occupancy load certificate, emergency lighting, and first aid provision) from the Employment and Safety Department of the Welfare and Labour Authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Ministry of Finance); online e-Tax portal at https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation; entity registration with Companies House Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Gibraltar-recognised Exempted Limited Partnership, once registered with Companies House Gibraltar under the Limited Partnerships Act 1991, must apply to the Income Tax Office for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number. The partnership is not separately taxable; each general and limited partner must obtain an individual Tax Reference Number and file a tax return in respect of their allocated share of partnership income. Foreign partners with no Gibraltar place of residence or business must appoint a Gibraltar tax-resident representative or agent authorised to receive assessments and service of documents. The application must include the registered partnership certificate, partnership agreement, beneficial ownership schedule, certified constitutional documents, and evidence of economic substance in Gibraltar if Gibraltar-source income is expected. Since Gibraltar does not impose VAT/GST, no separate VAT registration TIN is required; however, a Gibraltar EORI number must be obtained from the Gibraltar Customs and Excise Department if goods will be imported or exported.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. A limited partnership is mandatorily tax transparent under the Income Tax Act, with partners assessed individually on their agreed profit shares. Statutory allocations and special profit-sharing elections in the partnership agreement are respected for tax purposes. There is no elective corporate classification for an ELP. Hybrid mismatch rules under the OECD/G20 Base Erosion and Profit Shifting framework are implemented in Gibraltar, and an ELP participating in a mixed-status structure must comply with any required recharacterisation of deductions or income; no elective opt-out is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT / No GST / No General Sales Tax — Gibraltar operates a limited customs and excise duty system on specified goods (tobacco, alcohol, fuel) and imposes no broad-based indirect tax on goods or services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — Gibraltar imposes no VAT/GST, so there is no economic turnover threshold triggering indirect tax registration. Any person importing goods into or exporting goods from Gibraltar must obtain a Gibraltar EORI number and register with the Customs and Excise Department before the first dutiable transaction; there is no monetary threshold for that registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — Gibraltar does not mandate real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal data clearance, API transmission, or digital stamping. Customs entries are filed electronically through the Gibraltar Customs Single Administrative Document (SAD) portal, and standard commercial invoices are sufficient for customs and tax purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Gibraltar has no VAT/GST, therefore exports are outside the scope of indirect taxation rather than zero-rated. A taxable person may obtain relief or drawback of any customs and excise duties paid at import where goods are subsequently physically exported from Gibraltar to a non-Gibraltar destination. The exporter must demonstrate that the goods left Gibraltar, that consideration was received from a non-resident customer, and that the transaction was not part of a circular or artificial arrangement. Services supplied to non-residents for use wholly outside Gibraltar are not subject to any Gibraltar indirect tax and require no refund mechanism because no input VAT or GST is chargeable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Entry / Single Administrative Document (SAD)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR carrier proof of export
Customs Duty Drawback Claim Form (where applicable)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT payment statement evidencing receipt of funds from the overseas customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar Customs and Excise Department may audit all export and drawback documentation. False statements, forged export proofs, or circular transactions give rise to forfeiture of goods, a monetary penalty of up to the greater of GIP 5,000 or 150% of the duty evaded, retrospective clawback of all relief or drawback obtained, and potential criminal liability for fraudulent evasion of customs duty. In parallel, the Income Tax Office may disallow associated deductions, impose interest and penalties for under-declared taxable income, and apply Gibraltar’s economic substance and anti-abuse rules to recharacterise sham transactions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) as prudential banking regulator; monetary policy and exchange-control competence retained by the Bank of England and the Government of Gibraltar, with the Government of Gibraltar issuing the Gibraltar pound (GIP) under the Currency Notes Act 1934.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: GIP is pegged at par to GBP and is unconditionally convertible; Gibraltar maintains no exchange-control regime and imposes no restrictions on current-account or capital-account transactions. For a charitable endowment ELP, inbound donations, investment income, grant distributions and capital remittances do not require central bank approval. Convertibility friction arises only from sanctions screening, anti-money laundering verification and CRS/FATCA tax-transparency reporting, not from statutory currency barriers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Gibraltar has no statutory export-proceeds surrender, repatriation or mandatory conversion requirements. The charitable endowment is free to hold, convert and disburse inbound donation flows in GIP, GBP or any freely convertible currency; no exchange control mandate applies to grant receipts or to US/UK/EU source funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility as a secondary, non-custodial rail only. Revolut Business and Wise Business accept Gibraltar-registered companies but reject fiduciary, escrow, and charitable-endowment retention accounts and impose material caps on charitable payout flows. Gibraltar does not maintain a distinct EMI licensing class; following Brexit, EEA EMIs no longer passport automatically into Gibraltar and any e-money service must obtain authorisation under the Financial Services Act 2019 (Gibraltar). The ELP must not hold endowment principal, donor capital or escrowed grant funds in an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: GFSC-regulated banks require at least one natural-person general partner or a designated director of the corporate general partner to attend an in-person interview at the bank's Gibraltar office, unless an introducer relationship with an existing GFSC-licensed law firm or fiduciary enables remote video verification; purely remote onboarding for an offshore exempted limited partnership is not accepted in practice. Additionally, at least one of the two authorised signatories should have UK, EEA or Gibraltar residency to satisfy correspondent-bank de-risking policies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through ELP structure with non-resident limited partners and undisclosed ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised register of beneficial owners filed under the Gibraltar Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2017; complete limited partnership agreement; UBO chart identifying every 25% or greater economic-interest holder; passports and proof-of-address for all partners and controllers; GFSC-accredited anti-money laundering legal opinion; statutory declaration that no nominee or bearer shareholding exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous charitable status for a private foundation conducting endowment management
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registration certificate from the Gibraltar Charities Commissioner under the Charities Act 1961 (as amended); foundation deed and endowment trust deed demonstrating exclusively charitable objects; investment-management policy; annual budget and five-year cash-flow projections; independent Gibraltar legal opinion confirming no private profit motive; explicit confirmation that the ISIC 6430 grant-making activity does not constitute commercial trading.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large cross-border donations originating from foreign trusts, private foundations or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Donor gift letters and trust instruments; source-of-wealth files with audited financial statements or public tax records; UK Gift Aid direction or US 501(c)(3) equivalency letter where applicable; banker's reference from the donor's bank; independent reputation and sanctions database searches covering the donor, its principals and its jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate onward grant distribution to unvetted third-country grantees immediately after account opening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved grantee KYC file for each beneficiary comprising registration or charity status certificate, director and officer list, bank confirmation and sanctions screening; signed grant agreements referencing disbursement milestones; annual grant-risk matrix; pre-negotiated monthly disbursement threshold with the bank; written commitment to file suspicious transaction reports under the Gibraltar AML Act 2021 and a prohibition on cash or bearer-instrument payments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound donations and endowment capital injections must be received into the named Capital Escrow Account via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV where a correspondent bank handles cover). Each message must use the ISO 20022 purpose code 'CHAR' (charity) or 'GIFT' and carry the ELP's Gibraltar Companies House registration number and permanent-endowment reference in fields 70/72. The remitter and payee names must exactly match the KYC profile with no third-party interposition; donor banks must be licensed in the UK, EEA, Gibraltar or another FATF-equivalent jurisdiction. Any single donation exceeding GBP 250,000 triggers enhanced due diligence, CRS-relevant tax disclosure certificates and confirmation from the donor's bank of the lawful origin of funds; all receipts must be reconciled in a segregated grant-receivable ledger before any investment or disbursement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Grant distributions settle through SWIFT MT103 with MT202 COV covering for USD and EUR wires; UK grantees are paid via CHAPS or Faster Payments; EEA grantees via SEPA with the grant agreement identifier in the end-to-end reference field; USD grantees via the bank's New York correspondent through CHIPS or Fedwire. Procurement-linked scientific-grant contracts may additionally be secured by an MT700 documentary letter of credit issued by Jyske Bank where a grantee requires trade-settled payment against milestones. Every outbound payment must cite the grant agreement number, apply the ISO 20022 purpose code 'CHAR', 'GIFT' or 'COMC' as appropriate, and be screened against OFAC, EU and UN sanctions lists; grantees resident in restricted or high-risk jurisdictions require prior board and GFSC-relevant approval together with enhanced counterparty KYC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (GIP/USD, GIP/EUR, GBP/USD, GBP/EUR) with tenors up to 24 months executed with Jyske Bank or Turicum Private Bank as counterparty.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (GBP/USD and GBP/EUR) used solely for duration-matching and currency alignment of the endowment portfolio, capped at 10% of net asset value.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in non-convertible grant-currency exposures such as CNY, INR and NGN executed through Jyske's London desk; strictly no leverage and no extension beyond 12 months.

European-style FX options with upfront premium paid for protection on USD/EUR-denominated grant pipelines; leveraged, exotic or speculative derivative instruments are prohibited by the foundation's investment policy and the GFSC suitability requirements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: ELP Annual Return (Form LP-AR) confirming the registered office, registered agent, general partner and the schedule of limited partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar (Register of Limited Partnerships)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 28 days after each anniversary of the date of registration under the Limited Partnerships Act 2019.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GBP 50 per month of default, capped at GBP 500; continuation of default beyond 12 months obliges the Registrar to publish a strike-off notice in the Gibraltar Gazette and to proceed with administrative dissolution of the ELP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Charitable/Endowment Tax-Exempt Status (Form CIT-EX/RN) evidencing qualifying philanthropic purpose and grant payout compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January for the tax year ending on the previous 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted renewal withdraws the charitable exemption from the start of that assessment year, charging 12.5% Gibraltar corporation tax on endowment income with interest at 8% per annum; repeated failure triggers revocation of charitable status and referral to the Gibraltar Charities Commissioner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Charity Information Return (File CH-AR) including grant distribution schedule and externally reviewed financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Charities Commissioner, Civil Status and Registration Office, Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the 31 December financial year end, therefore on or before 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing suspends grant-making authority, instructs banking institutions to freeze the endowment's distribution account, and renders the foundation's controllers disqualified for up to 5 years under the Charities Act (Cap. 121).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Statement (BO-CS) attesting all partners holding 25% or more of capital, profits or voting rights
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Register Section, Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 21 days following each registration anniversary, aligned with the Form LP-AR filing cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm attracts a fine of up to GBP 5,000 and the Registrar may issue a restriction notice that suspends the transferability and economic rights of the relevant partnership interests until the filing is remedied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Compliance Return designating the Money Laundering Reporting Officer and confirming the risk assessment for grant distribution activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Intelligence Unit, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January for the immediately preceding calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalties of up to GBP 20,000 per deficient notice under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and the Gibraltar AML/CFT Subsidiary Regulations 2020; willful neglect may also result in a regulatory referral to the Gibraltar Coordinating Body for Serious and Organised Crime.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A pure ELP has no automatic statutory audit; independent audit becomes compulsory when (a) the entity is registered as a charity with annual gross income exceeding GBP 50,000; (b) the foundation is authorised by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission to conduct investment, fund or trust services; or (c) the general partner's accounts cross the Companies Act 2014 thresholds of turnover over GBP 6.5 million, balance sheet assets over GBP 3.26 million and more than 50 average employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted in Gibraltar under the Companies Act 2014, supplemented by the Charities (Accounts and Reports) Regulations 2021 for grant revenue recognition and related party disclosures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each anniversary the ELP must reconfirm its beneficial ownership register with the Registrar. Any transfer of a partnership interest resulting in a new beneficial owner holding 25% or more of capital, profits or voting rights requires an updated BO filing within 14 days of the transfer, regardless of the annual confirmation cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners' Capital Contributions
Register of General Partner and Controllers
Minute Book and statutory corporate records held at the Gibraltar registered office

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 - 3,500 per annum for a licensed Gibraltar registered agent covering the registered office, annual return preparation and custody of statutory registers
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 7,000 per annum for an IFRS-compliant independent audit of a small charitable endowment ELP engaging an approved Gibraltar audit firm
